3. Pursuant to said order the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Chittagong by order contained in Memo No. 362/1(6)/RM dated 28-10-1996 appointed Mr Helal Mahmud Sharif, the Assistant Commissioner, Chittagong to execute eviction proceeding and hand over the vacant possession to the petitioner who in his turn by letter in Memo 1536(B)/1/JM dated 3-12-1996 directed the Deputy Police Commissioner (North) Chittagong Metropolitan Police, Sadar, to arrange necessary police force on 30-12-1996 for executing the eviction proceeding. The said date of execution of the eviction proceeding was refaxed on 9-1-97 on which day some illegal trespassers from the land covered under BS Khatian No. 2908, BS Plot Nos 139/140/141 were evicted and possession was handed over of the same to the Petitioners-Mutwalli and submitted his report under Memo, No 81(8)JM dated 19-1-97. On 20-1-97 Manjur Ahmed the respondent No. 2 filed an application before the Administrator of Waqf, Dhaka under'' section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance claiming property in BS Khatian No 2937 BS Plot No.124 /12 5/126/1141/1142/1143/1145/1261/1262/ 23603 /23604 of Mouza-Bakalia stating that the said property has nothing to do with the property of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate bearing EC No.2059 (Chittagong) and prayed for withdrawal of the eviction order. The said application was registered as Waqf Miscellaneous Case No 29 of 1996 and Administrator of Waqf respondent No.1 by the impugned order dated 22-1-97 stayed the eviction proceeding pending final decision and for maintaining status quo. 

 4. The respondent No 2 contested the Rule filing Affidavit-in-Opposition stating, inter alia, that the schedule of the petitioner Waqf Estate as stated in the application by the petitioner for eviction is not true and correct. The lands of schedule-2 of the petition being plot No 311, 314, 315, 316, 317, 318, 320, 321, 322, 323, 324, 325, 326, 336, 337, 338, 339, 340, 341, 342, 343, 344, 345, 346, 347, 348, 350, 351, 353, 354 are not the property of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate. These are the property of Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate created on 5-10-28 being the subject matter of EC No 1690 of which the respondent and his two brothers are joint Mutwallis. The petitioner suppressed the same without impleading the respondent in the application have illegally sought to evict the respondent No 2 from the said plots which are recorded In the name of Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate in RS and BS operation. The present BS Plots in respect of those RS Plots also recorded in the name of respondent and his brother Mutwalli. Some of the property stood in their personal names and all the plots are in their possession. The respondent further asserted that the land appertaining to BS Khatian No.2935, 683, 2937, 2938 belong to the respondent and their Waqf Estate in the Khatian standing in their names. The respondent has further denied that 2.67 acres of land of EC No. 2059 or any other land has been forcibly possessed by trespassers. The petitioner''s claim in the petition under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance is not true but a misrepresentation of fact for obtaining illegal possession under the Waqf Ordinance. On 9-1-97 the respondent could learn about the illegal proceeding when all on a sudden the Magistrate went on the land belonging to the respondent Waqf Estate. The impugned action of eviction of alleged trespassers having been conducted behind the back of respondent No. 2 designed to illegally take over possession of land belonging to the respondent No. 2''s Waqf Property under the garb of section 64(1) of the Ordinance, was done without notifying persons concerned and without determining as to whether the land actually belongs to the petitioner's said Waqf Estate or whether the occupiers are trespassers or not. The respondent has further submitted that the said ex parte order of eviction of alleged trespassers without ascertaining and determining as to whether the land belongs to Waqf Estate of the petitioner or whether the occupiers are trespassers thereto, the order of eviction was wholly without jurisdiction and the Waqf Administrator did not commit any illegality or has not acted without jurisdiction in staying further proceeding of the eviction pending decision on the application under 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance. During the pendency of the Rule an application for addition of party as respondent No. 3 on behalf of the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong was filed and moved and this Court by order dated 27-5-97 directed that the application be kept on record to be disposed of at the time of hearing of the Rule. However the said application was not pressed at the time of hearing and accordingly, the said application is rejected as not pressed. 

 8. It appears from Annexure-C, a copy of the application under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 wherein the petitioner has stated that few days back he has been appointed as a Mutwalli and the land mentioned in the schedule thereto are in illegal possession of the persons namely, Manjur Ahmed (respondent No 2), Abu Taher and Nasir Uddin, sons of Munshi Azizur Rahman of West Bakalia, DC Road, PS Chandgaon, Chittagong and the petitioner tried to recover possession but said persons denying the right of Waqf Estate in schedule land have constructed many houses and the said illegal acts were done due to the callousness of the previous Mutwalli and if the trespassers are evicted, the income of the Waqf Estate will be enhanced to a great extent. The schedule of land mentioned the lands of CS Plots No 311/314/316/317/318/320/321/322/323/324/325/326/336/337/338/339/340/341/342/343/344/345/346/347/348/350/351/353/354 with an area of 6 kani 13 Ganda 2 Kara and the houses standing on some of these plots. On receipt of the said application on 17-5-96 the Waqf Administrator by his Memo No 268/Chittagong dated 1-9-96 addressed the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong requesting to take necessary action under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 in respect of the mentioned Waqf Estate (Annexure-D). It further appears from Annexure-E a letter issued by Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Chittagong addressed to Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate of the office of Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong contained in Memo No 362/1/(6)/RM dated 28-10-96 directing him to evict the illegal trespassers from the schedule land mentioned therein and to hand over possession to the petitioner giving the schedule described as BS Khatian No.2935, BS Dag No.195, 196,93,94.95, 113, 114, 122, 123, 129, 130, 136,138, 142, 113/322 BS Khatian No 683, 13S Dag No 111, 129, 130 139, 136, 137, 138, 142, 113/323'' B S Khatian No. 2938, B/S Dag No.127, 128, 139, 145, 141, BS Khatian No. 882 BS Dag No.21, BS Rhatian No.3234, BS Dag No 17, BS Khatian No. 722 BS Dag No 17 BS Khatian No 3345, BS Dag No 19.20, 16/321 BS Khatian Khatian No 1620, BS Dag No. 18. Neither the said Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate nor the Waqf Administrator nor the Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) or the Additional Deputy Commissioner issued any notice upon the alleged trespassers including the respondent No 2 to ascertain the fact of trespass and illegal construction on their part in the disputed lands by the alleged trespassers and themselves also did not ascertain as to whether the lands belong to the said Waqf Estate or that the occupiers are trespassers therein or not. But it appears from Annexure-H being Memo No. 81(4)/JM dated 19-1-97 of the Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate addressed to the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong allegedly stating that by holding eviction proceeding in part he has handed over possession of plot No.139, 140 and 141 of BS Khatian No 2938 to the petitioner, Mutwalli of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate. There are good numbers of timber shop, saloons, Pharmacy, Grocers shop and restaurants and the shop owners on the said plot have executed stamps of Taka 50.(X) (fifty) admitting that they are the tenants under the Waqf Estate. 

 10. It has been submitted, on our query, by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that in spite of the stay order passed by this Court no further action in the matter of eviction was conducted, instead the Deputy Commissioner himself wanted to be a party to the Rule by an application moved in this Court on 27-5-97, disposed of earlier in this judgment. In the said application on behalf of the Deputy Commissioner for impleading as respondent No 3 it has been stated that the Administrator of Waqf upon an application under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance for recovery of the possession of the Waqf land from illegal and unauthorized trespassers and on proper scrutiny the Administrator of Waqf by his order under Memo No 267/Chatta dated 1-9-96 ordered the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong to evict the unauthorized occupiers and possessors from the Waqf land bearing EC No 2059 (Chittagong) and in view of the order dated 1-9-96, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Chittagong by order dated 28-10-96 appointed Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate to execute eviction proceeding and hand over the vacant possession to the petitioner and consequently Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate by his letter under Memo No 1536(8)1/JM dated 3-12-96 requested the Deputy Police Commissioner (W) Chittagong Metropolitan Police, Sadar to arrange necessary police force for evicting the trespassers and on 9-1-97 unauthorized occupiers and possessors were evicted from land covered under BS Khatian No. 2908 BS Plot No. 139/140/141 and handed over possession to the petitioner. It appears from the schedule to the waqf deed (Annexure-A) that the waqf land have been described with reference to CS Plots as aforesaid, similarly, the petitioner in his application Annexure ''C'' under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance described the Waqf land with reference to said CS Plots of Mouza-Bakalia Police Station Panchalaish, District-Chittagong without mentioning the CS Khatian thereof with areaf of 6 Kani 13 Ganda 2 Kara with houses and buildings standing on part thereof and it would appear from Annexure-D dated 1-9-96 that the respondent No.1 has referred the said application dated 12-5-96 for necessary action to the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong but it appears from the Annexure-E, that on 28-10-96 Additional Deputy Commissioner directed the Assistant Commissioner/and Magistrate to make over possession of certain lands described with reference to CS Khatian and BS Plots by evicting the unauthorized occupants to the Mutwalli of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate. It further appears from Annexure-F that said Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate, Sadar fixed 30-12-96 for making over delivery of possession to the said Mutwalli by evicting the unauthorized occupiers from the waqf land described with reference to certain BS Khatians and BS Plots without any specification and boundary thereof. The quantum of land has not been stated therein and from Annexure-H, the report of that Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate it appears that eviction of alleged trespassers have been carried out from some part of the disputed land particularly from plots Nos.139, 149, 141 of BS Khatian No.2398 and handed over alleged possession to the Mutwalli of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate. 

 14. Section 36 of the Ordinance authorizes the Administrator to delegate his power to the Deputy Commissioner for the purpose of investigating and determining the nature and extent of Waqf and Waqf properties and the Administrator may also require the Deputy Commissioner to have an inspection of properties of a Waqf enrolled or make enquiries with regard to any matter relating to such waqf and the Deputy Commissioner can make such inquiry himself or through an officer subordinate to him. Thus section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance provides that if a co-sharer in waqf property or an individual beneficiary or any other person interested in a Waqf or a stranger, created disturbance or obstruction in the peaceful management of waqf or disturbed the possession'' of a Waqf Property by the MutWalli or committed trespass on any such property, the Administrator shall apply to the Deputy Commissioner who shall evict the trespassers or take such steps for preventing such disturbance or obstruction as he may deem fit. So under section 64(1) the Administrator of Waqf has been empowered to direct the Deputy Commissioner to evict the trespassers or take such step for preventing such disturbance or obstruction as he may deem fit. According to said section, in our view, while evicting the trespassers, a duty is cast upon the Administrator to ascertain the trespass, the person involved therein and the disputed land in question which has been trespassed. This he could do himself under section 27 by investigating and determining the nature and extent of waqf and waqfs properties and the persons involved in the said waqf property committing trespass. He can, however, delegate his power to the Deputy Commissioner of the District for investigating and determining the nature and extent of waqf and waqfs properties by way of an inspection or inquiry into any other matter relating to the waqf to be made by Deputy Commissioner by himself or through an official subordinate to him. In the instant facts and circumstances as detailed above, upon receipt of application of the petitioner dated 12-5-97 the Waqf Administrator without investigating and determining the extent and nature of waqf and waqf properties and without ascertaining the trespass, the persons involved and the disputed land in question as to the alleged trespass was into a good number of CS Plots of Mouza-Bakalia, PS Chandgaon and without ascertaining by way of enquiry and investigation and inspection either by himself and  through the Deputy Commissioner or official subordinate to him has referred the application to the. Deputy Commissioner for necessary action by his Memo dated 1-9-95 and without any order of Deputy Commissioner, the Additional Deputy Commission and the Commissioner and Magistrate have caused eviction of alleged trespassers from certain BS Plots under BS Khatian. The waqf deed and the application dated 12-5-97 described the waqf land in terms of CS Plots but meanwhile two more surveys named RS and BS have occurred. Admittedly no survey or repayment has been made as to the CS Plots appearing in the Waqf deed and the application dated 12-5-97 with BS Plots of BS Khatians, suddenly appearing in the Memo of Additional Deputy Commissioner and Magistrate for the first time in order to carry out the eviction of the alleged trespassers from the land and building standing on the good numbers of BS Plots without any demarcation and/or specification as to boundary. It is very clear from the Memo dated 1-9-96 issued by the Waqf Administrator in favour of the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong that there was absolutely no order for eviction of the alleged trespasser but was directed to take necessary action under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance. But the Deputy Commissioner without determining or investigating into the matter as required under the law mechanically directed Additional Deputy Commissioner to effect eviction as stated above. Moreover, there is neither any enquiry nor any inspection or any investigation and determination as to the nature and extent of the waqf and waqf property for evicting the alleged trespassers on the disputed land in question which has been trespassed. The process of eviction as has been done, have no sanction of law. The impugned order goes to show that the Waqf Administrator has passed the order of ''status quo'' and stayed the further proceeding of order of eviction till the matter is finally decided by the Waqf Administrator. Under section 21 of the General Clauses Act the authority, the Waqf Administrator could as well stay the order of eviction directing status quo and stay of further proceeding of eviction process even if assuming that by his Memo dated 1-9-96 the Waqf Administrator has ordered the Deputy Commissioner to carry out the eviction of the trespassers pending disposal of the said application.
